C.3.2 Collection and Mature Handoff

Mature episodes and collection sets.

A root entry into 𝖶𝗈𝗋𝗄\mathsf{Work} at round c0c_{0} is mature if, after round-start transitions, every other player is in armed 𝖲𝖾𝖾𝗄\mathsf{Seek}, BUS\mathrm{BUS} uses control service, every non-BUS\mathrm{BUS} arm has started and was empty in the preceding two rounds, and no old work invocation or replay remains. The root’s invocation and those following it form a mature episode. Players do not test maturity.

The analysis tracks a growing collection set. At its starting round vv, include every present player except those in non-BUS\mathrm{BUS} replay; in particular, include old 𝖶𝗈𝗋𝗄\mathsf{Work} players and BUS\mathrm{BUS} replayers. Excluded players join when their replays end and remain thereafter. Before the first work entry under consideration, the set contains every BUS\mathrm{BUS} requester, giving its highest member priority on ordinary control visits. A higher external join adds a player above that member; it is a collection-set entry by an already present player, not a market arrival.

Control service and the work handoff.
Lemma 11 (Control service and the highest collector).

In control service, a continuous requester is accepted within K​GLKG_{L} rounds, and an alternating requester within 2​K​GL2KG_{L} rounds. An old business lease adds at most τL\tau_{L} rounds if requests leave no two consecutive empty rounds.

Once control service is in effect, the highest member of a collection set containing every actual BUS\mathrm{BUS} requester cannot receive KK consecutive rejections on its continuous or alternating BUS\mathrm{BUS} visits. Its presence also prevents a lower collector from obtaining three consecutive physical-round acceptances at BUS\mathrm{BUS}.

Proof.

Until its first acceptance, the requester’s timestamp stays fixed. Any player accepted ahead of it on a fair round acquires a newer timestamp and cannot precede it again on a fair round. Acceptance thus takes at most KK fair rounds on which it requests. These occur every GLG_{L} rounds for a continuous requester and, since GLG_{L} is odd, every 2​GL2G_{L} rounds for an alternating requester. Either pattern prevents lease renewal, so an old lease expires within τL\tau_{L} rounds.

The highest collector wins every ordinary control visit. Even with alternating visits, ordinary visits separate successive fair visits, preventing K≥2K\geq 2 consecutive rejections. If a lower collector is accepted at tt, the higher collector visits in t+1t+1 or t+2t+2. On an ordinary visit priority blocks the lower player; on a fair visit the higher player’s timestamp predates the lower player’s acceptance at tt. A higher player joining from an excluded non-BUS\mathrm{BUS} replay has no BUS\mathrm{BUS} acceptance during collection, so its first request also interrupts any acceptance suffix begun during collection. These arguments use the private order, independently of reward preferences. ∎

Lemma 12 (Mature handoff and service intervals).

If a mature root enters 𝖶𝗈𝗋𝗄\mathsf{Work} at c0c_{0}, each of the nn players enters exactly once at ci∈[c0,c0+κL]c_{i}\in[c_{0},c_{0}+\kappa_{L}], outputs at Oi=ci+JL−1O_{i}=c_{i}+J_{L}-1, and reaches first common replay at S=maxi⁡Oi+1S=\max_{i}O_{i}+1. Every arm uses business service from the first nonparking work round c0+dLc_{0}+d_{L} through S+χLS+\chi_{L}.

The common interval

I0=[c0+κL+hD,L,c0+fL)∩ℤI_{0}=[c_{0}+\kappa_{L}+h_{D,L},\,c_{0}+f_{L})\cap\mathbb{Z} (54)

contains WLW_{L} rounds, throughout which every player is within its deletion window and has not passed its certification cutoff. Every actual deletion window, including those outside I0I_{0}, consists entirely of held or cooled exploratory requests by all players, with none parking or replaying.

Proof.

Bound the entry span. After the root leaves BUS\mathrm{BUS}, armed followers enter in its private order: three consecutive ordinary acceptances transfer the highest remaining follower. A fair rejection can break at most two acceptances, delaying entry by at most three rounds; it cannot interrupt the sole remaining follower.

Between interruptions, GL−1=2​K+2G_{L}-1=2K+2 ordinary rounds permit at least ⌊(2​K+2)/3⌋\lfloor(2K+2)/3\rfloor transfers. Three interruptions would require 2​⌊(2​K+2)/3⌋≥K−22\lfloor(2K+2)/3\rfloor\geq K-2 transfers before the third, leaving at most one follower and ruling it out. For K=2K=2, the sole follower needs at most three rounds. For 3≤K≤53\leq K\leq 5, at most one interruption gives 3​K≤4​K−33K\leq 4K-3 rounds. For K≥6K\geq 6, the bound is 3​(K−1)+6≤4​K−3=κL3(K-1)+6\leq 4K-3=\kappa_{L}.

Maintain business service and identify the common window. Write δ=maxi⁡ci−c0≤κL\delta=\max_{i}c_{i}-c_{0}\leq\kappa_{L}. Since dL=κL+2d_{L}=\kappa_{L}+2, all players park at both c0+κLc_{0}+\kappa_{L} and c0+κL+1c_{0}+\kappa_{L}+1, refreshing the empty BUS\mathrm{BUS}’s lease. Other arms had two empty rounds just before c0c_{0}. Even this earlier refresh need cover only JL+κL+χL+1=JL+2​χL<τLJ_{L}+\kappa_{L}+\chi_{L}+1=J_{L}+2\chi_{L}<\tau_{L} rounds through S+χLS+\chi_{L}; later empty pairs can renew it. The identity fL−κL−hD,L=WLf_{L}-\kappa_{L}-h_{D,L}=W_{L} proves the claims about I0I_{0}.

Check deletion and certification endpoints. A deletion at tt by player ii uses a KK-rejection run starting no earlier than ci+hD,Lc_{i}+h_{D,L}, because the counter clears outside that window. Every other player’s work index throughout the run is at least hD,L−κL=χL+2>dLh_{D,L}-\kappa_{L}=\chi_{L}+2>d_{L}, and

t≤ci+fL−1≤c0+κL+fL−1=c0+JL−2<minj⁡Oj.t\leq c_{i}+f_{L}-1\leq c_{0}+\kappa_{L}+f_{L}-1=c_{0}+J_{L}-2<\min_{j}O_{j}.

Thus none is parking or has reached output or replay, and the action rule cools every nonholding request, including fillers.

The latest certification is by c0+κL+fL=c0+JL−1=mini⁡Oic_{0}+\kappa_{L}+f_{L}=c_{0}+J_{L}-1=\min_{i}O_{i}, before that round’s feedback. Also, mini⁡Oi+HL≥maxi⁡Oi+2=S+1\min_{i}O_{i}+H_{L}\geq\max_{i}O_{i}+2=S+1, so minimum grace prevents fresh entry until every player has completed round SS. ∎

From collection to mature entry.

Clearing places scan acceptances after earlier replays’ minimum grace, allowing recall. Suppose a highest collector enters fresh 𝖲𝖾𝖾𝗄\mathsf{Seek} at ww. Another player’s work entry at l≤w+2l\leq w+2 outputs at l+JL−1l+J_{L}-1, with minimum replay deadline l+JL+χLl+J_{L}+\chi_{L}, at least two rounds before the initial clearing deadline w+JL+χL+4w+J_{L}+\chi_{L}+4. An entry l≥w+3l\geq w+3 before root nomination requires actual BUS\mathrm{BUS} acceptances at l−3,l−2,l−1l-3,l-2,l-1. The continuously requesting collector is rejected in all three rounds; the last rejection sets clearing to at least l+JL+χL+2l+J_{L}+\chi_{L}+2, again two rounds after minimum grace. After nomination, Lemma 11 prevents lower players’ work entries.

Thus scanning starts after all old work and minimum grace. Old BUS\mathrm{BUS} replayers have already entered fresh: of the collector’s last two pre-scan BUS\mathrm{BUS} requests, at least one wins ordinary control service and rejects them after grace. If root entry skips clearing, its nomination acceptances suffice. The two-round margin covers a pending transition. At each other arm, the scan acceptance rejects all old replayers after grace, making them fresh next round.

Let ss be the last non-BUS\mathrm{BUS} scan acceptance. All recalled players are fresh by s+1s+1, and the latest guard occupies s+1,…,s+ELs+1,\ldots,s+E_{L}. Commitment starts at s+1s+1 and lasts at least EL+KE_{L}+K rounds, making its final KK rounds post-guard; its final acceptance suffix gives every recalled seeker KK rejections. An inherited root may start this suffix scanning off BUS\mathrm{BUS}, but its KKth rejected BUS\mathrm{BUS} visit occurs by suffix round 2​K2K, followed by armed 𝖲𝖾𝖾𝗄\mathsf{Seek}. Thus all players are at BUS\mathrm{BUS} in the last two rounds of the Rc,L=2​K+1R_{c,L}=2K+1 suffix. Every other arm has been started by the scan and is empty in both rounds. Such a suffix is available because GL−1=2​K+2≥Rc,LG_{L}-1=2K+2\geq R_{c,L}.

This proves maturity when the final highest player completes collection after fresh entry, and will also apply to the first work entry after mature common replay. It need not hold for an arbitrary inherited lower root.

Lemma 13 (An output time bound for the highest collector).

Fix a population and a history reached from the prescribed initialization. Let zz be the highest present player or the highest member of a collection set begun at vv. By v+C0v+C_{0}, either zz has an actual output or a higher external collector joins. An existing player’s output may be used; existing work has at most JLJ_{L} rounds left. For the highest present player, no higher external join is possible.

Proof.

Suppose zz initially seeks or is a root, and follow it until a higher external join. Until work entry, it covers BUS\mathrm{BUS} continuously or alternately. The elapsed-time allowances are summarized below and justified in order. If work starts earlier, only its fixed remaining duration is needed.

Stage Allowance in physical rounds
Expire the BUS lease and establish a root τL+EL+6\tau_{L}+E_{L}+6
Clear inherited work and minimum replay grace 2​(JL+χL+4)2(J_{L}+\chi_{L}+4)
Expire occupied-arm leases and finish the scan τL+Ls,L\tau_{L}+L_{s,L}
Commit and complete work EL+K+GL+Rc,L+JLE_{L}+K+G_{L}+R_{c,L}+J_{L}
Total C0−18C_{0}-18

Establish control service. The old BUS\mathrm{BUS} lease expires within τL\tau_{L} rounds. Set tc=v+τLt_{c}=v+\tau_{L} and t1=tc+EL+6t_{1}=t_{c}+E_{L}+6. A highest seeker finishes its guard within ELE_{L} rounds and obtains three consecutive acceptances within six more. An inherited root visits BUS by tc+1t_{c}+1; if its old rejection suffix causes demotion, it enters armed Seek by tc+2t_{c}+2 and work within six further rounds, costing 8≤EL+68\leq E_{L}+6. Otherwise an ordinary acceptance clears the suffix, and fair rejections cannot cause demotion. Hence by t1t_{1}, unless already working, zz is a root that cannot be demoted while highest, including by old work players in the collection set.

Clear old work and finish scanning. The fixed clearing deadline has at most JL+χL+4J_{L}+\chi_{L}+4 rounds left. Allow another JL+χL+4J_{L}+\chi_{L}+4 for foreign work and minimum grace: Lemma 11 excludes foreign work entries after tc+2t_{c}+2. By then no foreign work remains; while zz collects, no lower player can obtain a new root nomination or work entry. Each can finish at most one inherited root invocation, with at most (K−1)2(K-1)^{2} remaining non-BUS\mathrm{BUS} scan acceptances in total.

Another τL\tau_{L} rounds, shared across arms, expire leases still continuously occupied by old replayers; an earlier-ending replay needs no allowance. Put t2=t1+2​(JL+χL+4)+τLt_{2}=t_{1}+2(J_{L}+\chi_{L}+4)+\tau_{L}. Unless already working, zz is then scanning or committing, no foreign work remains, and arms still occupied by old replayers use control service. There, its scan succeeds within 2​K​GL2KG_{L} control rounds. At any other target, each rejection of zz is an actual non-BUS\mathrm{BUS} scan acceptance by an inherited root. Counting intervening BUS\mathrm{BUS} visits and zz’s own acceptances gives remaining scan time at most

2​K​GL​(K−1)+2​((K−1)2+(K−1))=Ls,L.2KG_{L}(K-1)+2\bigl((K-1)^{2}+(K-1)\bigr)=L_{s,L}.

This includes roots not yet demoted and each target’s preceding BUS visit, including its first. Target updates take no extra round; the last acceptance starts commitment next round.

Commit and output. Commitment takes at most EL+K+GL+Rc,LE_{L}+K+G_{L}+R_{c,L} rounds for its minimum duration and a full ordinary acceptance suffix, then work outputs within JLJ_{L} more. The allowances sum to

2​τL+2​EL+3​JL+2​χL+GL+Rc,L+Ls,L+K+14=C0−18.2\tau_{L}+2E_{L}+3J_{L}+2\chi_{L}+G_{L}+R_{c,L}+L_{s,L}+K+14=C_{0}-18.

They count elapsed physical rounds, with next-round transitions and output included in work, leaving eighteen spare rounds in C0C_{0} unless a higher external collector joins first. ∎

C.3.3 Cold and Warm Recovery

Cold recovery from inherited states.

Cold recovery covers every reachable state after stabilization, including those inherited from erroneous comparisons.

Lemma 14 (Cold recovery, simultaneously for every starting time).

On every execution from the prescribed initialization with a nonempty final population, for each integer v≥t∗+1v\geq t_{*}+1 there is a mature episode whose remaining sets are all reset after vv and whose common replay begins by

T⁡(v)≤32​v+CR.T(v)\leq\frac{3}{2}v+C_{R}. (55)

This holds simultaneously for all such vv, without statistical correctness.

Proof.

Obtain a fresh entry. For the final highest player zz at BUS\mathrm{BUS}, Lemma 13 gives an output O≤v+C0O\leq v+C_{0}, possibly its existing replay’s output. Lemma 10 and replay shortening then give a fresh entry w≥vw\geq v with

w≤32​(v+C0)+HL.w\leq\frac{3}{2}(v+C_{0})+H_{L}.

For existing replay use its actual expiry, processed at once if already due at vv; for collection or work at vv, use the next output and ensuing expiry. This output need not be mature: it only supplies fresh entry and discards inherited qualification.

Complete a mature collection. Fresh entry erases old armed qualification. Throughout the ELE_{L}-round guard, zz requests BUS\mathrm{BUS} continuously, expiring its old lease before qualification. It cannot then receive KK consecutive rejected control visits, so its next work follows its own root collection. Clearing, recall, and commitment make this entry mature: all old work and replay have ended, followers are armed, and every non-BUS\mathrm{BUS} arm was empty in the preceding two rounds.

Lemma 13 from ww, followed by Lemma 12, bounds common replay by

w+C0+κL+1≤32​v+52​C0+HL+κL+1≤32​v+CR.w+C_{0}+\kappa_{L}+1\leq\frac{3}{2}v+\frac{5}{2}C_{0}+H_{L}+\kappa_{L}+1\leq\frac{3}{2}v+C_{R}.

Every work reset is strictly after ww, hence after vv. The deterministic argument applies on each realized path to every integer vv, simultaneously, even when vv is not a stopping time. ∎

Warm recovery and consecutive actual outputs.

Mature common replay gives bounded collection and identifies each player’s next actual output.

Lemma 15 (Warm collection and adjacency of actual outputs).

Suppose a mature episode reaches common replay at SS and the population stays fixed. Let q0q_{0} be the first actual fresh entry after SS. The next episode is mature, with common replay S′S^{\prime} satisfying

S′−q0≤VB+K​C0+κL+1.S^{\prime}-q_{0}\leq V_{B}+KC_{0}+\kappa_{L}+1. (56)

Each player has exactly one new work invocation and actual output between these common replays, so that output uses its stored record from the preceding mature episode. This holds regardless of statistical errors or replay correctness.

Proof.

Recall BUS replayers. Lemma 12 gives q0≥S+1q_{0}\geq S+1. The first fresh player requests BUS\mathrm{BUS} continuously until accepted, by q0+τL+K​GLq_{0}+\tau_{L}+KG_{L} under residual business service and control fairness. This rejects every old BUS\mathrm{BUS} replayer. Each minimum grace deadline is at most S+χLS+\chi_{L}: rejection before grace sets that deadline by (51), and rejection after grace gives fresh entry next round. In either case every old BUS\mathrm{BUS} replayer is fresh by q0+VBq_{0}+V_{B}, even if several erroneous outputs replay BUS\mathrm{BUS}.

Establish maturity of the first new work entry. Until that entry, the growing collection set contains the old BUS\mathrm{BUS} replayers, all players already fresh, and hence every BUS\mathrm{BUS} requester. Unjoined players repeat fixed non-BUS\mathrm{BUS} outputs; no new output has returned anyone to replay. Replayers cannot qualify before becoming fresh, which resets their armed flags. A collector keeps covering BUS\mathrm{BUS}, preventing lease renewal, so every fresh guard ends after control service begins. The current highest collector has been highest since joining, as higher members cannot leave. After its guard it cannot become armed, while lower armed seekers cannot obtain three consecutive acceptances in its presence. A still higher join interrupts any such suffix on its joining round through its old BUS\mathrm{BUS} timestamp. Thus the first new work entry must follow root collection.

That root’s fresh guard and clearing put its scan after all old minimum grace deadlines. Its BUS\mathrm{BUS} and scan acceptances recall every old replayer, so all have joined by the round after the last scan acceptance. A higher collector would interrupt the final acceptance suffix; a completing root is therefore highest. Minimum commitment gives the last recalled seeker a full guard and KK subsequent rejections; the last 2​K+12K+1 acceptances demote residual roots and give two empty rounds at every other arm. The first work entry is mature.

Bound the time and identify adjacent outputs. After the initial VBV_{B} rounds, divide collection at higher external joins. Each raises the highest collector’s priority, giving at most KK segments. In each, Lemma 13 gives an output or higher join within C0C_{0} rounds. The last includes root work; Lemma 12 adds at most κL+1\kappa_{L}+1 rounds to common replay. Work beginning during the initial allowance also fits, with its fixed remainder and handoff. This proves (56).

No new output preceded the first work entry. Its mature handoff starts exactly one fixed-length invocation per player, and minimum grace prevents another fresh entry before S′S^{\prime}. Each player thus outputs exactly once; since only actual outputs update its persistent record, it uses exactly the preceding mature output’s record. ∎

C.4 Stable-Edge Protection, Absorption, and Sample Progress

The recovery guarantees above hold regardless of statistical errors. We now use comparison coverage to protect stable edges and identify the POSM, then introduce the sample threshold needed to charge failed episodes to permanent samples.

C.4.1 Comparison Coverage and Good Episodes

Writing θx\theta_{x} for the true mean of option xx, a positive-count comparison is covered when

|(θ^x−θ^z)−(θx−θz)|≤βa​(x,z).\left|(\widehat{\theta}_{x}-\widehat{\theta}_{z})-(\theta_{x}-\theta_{z})\right|\leq\beta_{a}(x,z). (57)

Under coverage of all comparisons in a nonempty set, its true best option cannot be excluded. A singleton confidence set therefore certifies that option.

An episode is good if all comparisons between each player’s KK arms and at each arm between present players are covered from the first remaining-set reset through the end of the first common replay round, including earlier certificates used by later deletion witnesses. It is successful if, at common replay, every player holds an arm and the saved outputs are distinct. Collection remains valid after incorrect statistical decisions.

C.4.2 Stable-Edge Protection and POSM Absorption

The POSM benchmark.

Player-proposing deferred acceptance yields the POSM in a finite strict market [GS62]. Rejection by all KK arms would require KK other retained players, impossible for n≤Kn\leq K. A first rejection of a stable edge would be caused by a preferred proposer whose own stable partner had not yet rejected it, yielding a blocking pair. Thus no stable edge is rejected. At termination, each player receives its best stable arm: every preferred arm rejected it and retains a better proposer. We use this characterization to identify SC-PC’s absorbing assignment.

Lemma 16 (A held witness for every deletion).

In a mature good episode, if player ii deletes arm aa, some other player jj whom aa prefers to ii held and requested aa during the KK-rejection window. The witness need not have been accepted in that window.

Proof.

The KK rejections of ii require KK acceptances among at most K−1K-1 other players. Some player ww is accepted twice, at arm ages r<sr<s with s−r≤K−1s-r\leq K-1. Lemma 12 excludes parking and replay; cooldown excludes an exploratory request by ww at ss. Thus ww holds aa. If aa prefers ww to ii, it is the required witness.

Otherwise let zz be aa’s best requester at ss. If z≠iz\neq i is a holder, it is the required witness. In the remaining cases, z=iz=i has been rejected throughout the window, or zz is exploring and has no acceptance at aa in the preceding K−1K-1 rounds. Just before service at ss, either case gives

last⁡[z]<r≤last⁡[w].\operatorname{last}[z]<r\leq\operatorname{last}[w].

Coverage keeps zz eligible, so oldest-timestamp service cannot select ww, a contradiction. No sample threshold or gap bound is needed. ∎

Lemma 17 (Stable-edge protection and absorption).

A mature good episode deletes no edge of any stable matching. Every held arm is weakly preferred by its holder to its POSM arm. If all players hold distinct arms, their assignment is the POSM and persists until the next collection. There are at most (n−1)2(n-1)^{2} deletions in an nn-player episode.

Proof.

Stable edges. Suppose (i,a)(i,a) is the first deleted stable edge, and fix a stable matching containing it. Lemma 16 gives a holder jj whom aa prefers to ii. At jj’s certification of aa, its partner in that matching remained available. Coverage makes aa its true best remaining arm, so (j,a)(j,a) blocks the matching. This also handles simultaneous deletions: all certificates use round-start sets, before feedback deletes any edge. Every stable edge is therefore protected; in particular, every held arm is at least as good for its holder as its still-available POSM arm.

Persistent holders and absorption. Before collection resumes, an arm’s best historical holder cannot have deleted it: a deletion witness would be an even better historical holder. Holding otherwise persists, including through output and replay, so every previously held arm retains a holder. If all players hold distinct arms, an arm preferred by a player to its current assignment must have been deleted before certification. Its witness, and hence its best historical holder, is preferred to that player by the arm. No deleted arm can be unoccupied. The assignment is therefore stable and weakly better for every player than the POSM, hence equal to it under strict preferences. With one requester per occupied arm, all subsequent requests are accepted until collection.

Deletion count. The first time nn distinct arms have been held, their persistent holders account for all nn players, giving absorption. Before then, deletions concern at most n−1n-1 ever-held arms. Each such arm’s best holder over the episode never deletes it, and each of the other players deletes it at most once. Thus there are at most (n−1)2(n-1)^{2} deletions. ∎

C.4.3 Samples Collected by Failed Episodes

Stable-edge protection uses full coverage alone; the restricted gap quantifies sample progress. For the nonempty final market, use Δmin\Delta_{\min} from (11). For an integer horizon T≥2T\geq 2, define the analysis threshold

QT=1+⌊40​Δmin−2​log⁡T⌋.Q_{T}=1+\left\lfloor 40\Delta_{\min}^{-2}\log T\right\rfloor. (58)

If a≤Ta\leq T and both counts are at least QTQ_{T}, then a+2≤T2a+2\leq T^{2} and log⁡(a+2)≤2​log⁡T\log(a+2)\leq 2\log T, so

βa​(x,z)≤10​log⁡TQT<Δmin2.\beta_{a}(x,z)\leq\sqrt{\frac{10\log T}{Q_{T}}}<\frac{\Delta_{\min}}{2}.

Under coverage, a gap of at least Δmin\Delta_{\min} then excludes the inferior option whenever the superior option is present. Neither QTQ_{T} nor the gap is a protocol input.

Fix a mature good episode of the final population with common replay by TT; all relevant ages are at most TT. An acceptance is insufficient if its edge count just before acceptance is below QTQ_{T}. Both endpoints have that same count. Recall Ei∗={x:μi,x≥μi,m∗​(i)}E_{i}^{*}=\{x:\mu_{i,x}\geq\mu_{i,m^{*}(i)}\}.

The sample argument has three steps. A target created before the certification cutoff must still need samples; otherwise the player would certify instead. A block without sample progress must then either delete an arm or reach the POSM. Since an episode permits only finitely many deletions, a failed episode must collect a fixed sample quota.

Lemma 18 (Fixed probe targets remain insufficiently sampled in the common window).

Every exploratory target maintained in I0I_{0} has player count below QTQ_{T}, even if it has left the current confidence set.

Proof.

Such a target was created before the player’s certification cutoff. Stable-edge protection keeps the remaining set nonempty; its true best arm lies in Ei∗E_{i}^{*} and remains a candidate. By (11), the player-side gap between that best arm and any inferior candidate is at least Δmin\Delta_{\min}. If all candidates had counts at least QTQ_{T}, coverage and (58) would let that best arm exclude every inferior candidate. The resulting singleton would be certified before target creation. Thus the least-sampled candidate selected as target has count below QTQ_{T}.

While retained, the target’s count cannot change: an accepted probe or a new certificate clears it, and a filler cannot request the uncooled target. The conclusion therefore holds even after the target leaves the confidence set. It need not hold for targets created after the certification cutoff. ∎

Lemma 19 (A cooled block and the amortized inequality).

Consider KK consecutive rounds in I0I_{0} with no insufficient acceptance in the block or the preceding K−1K-1 rounds. If the block contains no deletion, absorption at the POSM occurs by its last round. Consequently, every prefix II of I0I_{0} ending before absorption satisfies

|I|≤K​DI+(2​K−1)​BI+2​K−2,|I|\leq KD_{I}+(2K-1)B_{I}+2K-2, (59)

where DID_{I} and BIB_{I} count deletions and insufficient acceptances in II, respectively, with each accepted edge counted separately.

Proof.

A block with neither kind of event. At its first action, each player holds an arm, possibly certifying it then, or explores. An explorer’s target is insufficient by Lemma 18. Any acceptance at that target in the preceding K−1K-1 rounds would also have been insufficient, so the target is cooled. Every subsequent probe acceptance would be insufficient as well. Without acceptance or deletion, the player’s statistics and remaining set stay fixed; increasing age only widens the confidence radii, so a nonsingleton cannot become a singleton. The player therefore probes for KK rounds and deletes, a contradiction. All players must hold from their first action.

If two fixed holders share an arm, let zz be its true best requester, which remains eligible under coverage. If zz’s edge is insufficient, its timestamp cannot change without an insufficient acceptance. Each other requester can be served ahead of it at most once, so the arm accepts zz within KK rounds, a contradiction. If its edge is sufficient, every sufficient inferior holder is excluded: both held edges lie in the respective Ei∗E_{i}^{*} sets, so their arm-side gap is at least Δmin\Delta_{\min}. The block rules out insufficient acceptances, so the arm accepts only zz throughout it. Any inferior holder then deletes after KK rejections. Thus all held arms are distinct, and Lemma 17 gives absorption.

Charge the rounds before absorption. The block argument charges time either to deletions or to insufficient acceptances and their cooldowns. Mark the first K−1K-1 rounds of II and each insufficient-acceptance round together with its next K−1K-1 rounds, truncated at the endpoint. There are at most K​BI+K−1KB_{I}+K-1 marked rounds and at most BI+1B_{I}+1 unmarked intervals. Every disjoint KK-round block in an unmarked interval must contain a deletion; otherwise absorption would persist to the end of II. An interval with dd deletions thus has length at most K​d+K−1Kd+K-1. Summing gives

|I|≤K​BI+K−1+K​DI+(BI+1)​(K−1),|I|\leq KB_{I}+K-1+KD_{I}+(B_{I}+1)(K-1),

which is (59). The initial marks cover insufficient acceptances before II; subsequent cooldown is charged to insufficient acceptances within it. ∎

Lemma 20 (Sample density and the first fresh entry).

For the nonempty final market, fix T≥2T\geq 2 and the threshold QTQ_{T} from (58). Every failed mature good episode with common replay by TT contains at least bK=2​K2b_{K}=2K^{2} insufficient acceptances, and there are at most ⌊QT/2⌋\lfloor Q_{T}/2\rfloor such episodes.

For any mature good episode in a fixed population, let SS be its first common replay round. If the episode succeeds, it replays the POSM until the first fresh entry; if it fails, that entry occurs by S+χLS+\chi_{L}.

Proof.

Sample quota and failure count. Absorption during I0I_{0} persists through output and common replay, so a failed episode cannot be absorbed there. If it had at most bK−1b_{K}-1 insufficient acceptances in I0I_{0}, Lemma 17 and (59) would give

WL≤K​(K−1)2+(2​K−1)​(bK−1)+2​K−2=WL−1,W_{L}\leq K(K-1)^{2}+(2K-1)(b_{K}-1)+2K-2=W_{L}-1,

a contradiction. The permanent potential

ΦT=∑i∈𝒫∞∑a∈𝒦max⁡{0,QT−Ni​(a)}≤n​K​QT≤K2​QT\Phi_{T}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{P}_{\infty}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal{K}}\max\{0,Q_{T}-N_{i}(a)\}\leq nKQ_{T}\leq K^{2}Q_{T}

never increases and drops by one at each insufficient acceptance. Distinct mature episodes have disjoint common windows, so at most ⌊K2​QT/bK⌋=⌊QT/2⌋\lfloor K^{2}Q_{T}/b_{K}\rfloor=\lfloor Q_{T}/2\rfloor can fail, regardless of intervening successes or additional samples.

First fresh entry. By Lemma 12, certifications end by the earliest output’s action and deletions end strictly before it. Hence all output holders are already fixed at that action. In a successful episode, these fixed holders request distinct arms in every output round, so every final request is accepted and every output takes the long branch. If all outputs are long and distinct, the players hold the POSM, which persists until collection.

Otherwise, either a short output has deadline Oi+HL≤S+χLO_{i}+H_{L}\leq S+\chi_{L}, or two long outputs coincide and at least one is rejected at SS. Its shortened deadline satisfies

max⁡{S+1,Oi+HL}≤S+χL.\max\{S+1,O_{i}+H_{L}\}\leq S+\chi_{L}.

Thus a failed episode has a fresh entry by S+χLS+\chi_{L}, while minimum grace places every such entry after SS. ∎

C.5 Counting Episodes and Mismatch Cost

The preceding sample bound controls failures. We next bound mismatch between consecutive common replay rounds and use scale growth to count successes. Permanent counts and replay scales persist along the same consecutive chain.

Mismatch cost between common replay rounds.

Define the per-interval cost bound

CF\displaystyle C_{F} =K​C0+VB+κL+χL+16\displaystyle=KC_{0}+V_{B}+\kappa_{L}+\chi_{L}+16 (60)
=39​K4−19​K3+154​K2+10​K+4.\displaystyle=39K^{4}-19K^{3}+154K^{2}+10K+4.

The four terms charge collection, recall of BUS replayers, output misalignment, and the short delay before fresh entry; the remaining constant absorbs endpoints. Thus CF=O⁡(K4)C_{F}=O(K^{4}) bounds a whole interval between common replay rounds, including its final partial prefix.

Lemma 21 (At most CFC_{F} mismatched rounds in a warm interval).

Suppose a mature good episode reaches common replay at SS and the population remains fixed. If S′S^{\prime} is the next mature common replay, then

D⁡([S,S′),I)≤CF.D([S,S^{\prime});I)\leq C_{F}.

The bound also holds for every truncation [S,min⁡{S′,T})[S,\min\{S^{\prime},T\}), T>ST>S, including horizons inside the next collection or work invocation.

Proof.

Let q0q_{0} be the first fresh entry after SS. By Lemma 20, [S,q0)[S,q_{0}) has zero cost after success and length at most χL\chi_{L} after failure. Lemma 15 bounds the rest, regardless of the successor’s statistical correctness:

D⁡([S,S′),I)≤χL+(S′−q0)≤χL+VB+K​C0+κL+1≤CF.D([S,S^{\prime});I)\leq\chi_{L}+(S^{\prime}-q_{0})\leq\chi_{L}+V_{B}+KC_{0}+\kappa_{L}+1\leq C_{F}.

Truncation only reduces cost. Source goodness is essential: an incorrect injective replay may receive no rejection. Cold recovery will account for that case. ∎

Scale growth and the number of successes.
Lemma 22 (Minimum-scale growth after a successful episode).

Consider consecutive mature episodes s,s+1s,s+1 in a fixed population, with ss good and successful and s+1s+1 completed. Write

Oi,s=Os+δi,s,Os=mini⁡Oi,s,0≤δi,s≤κL,ps=mini⁡Pi,s,O_{i,s}=O_{s}+\delta_{i,s},\qquad O_{s}=\min_{i}O_{i,s},\qquad 0\leq\delta_{i,s}\leq\kappa_{L},\qquad p_{s}=\min_{i}P_{i,s},

where scales are measured after output. Even if the successor fails,

ps+1≥⌊5​ps+HL+2​(JL−κL−1)4⌋>54​ps.p_{s+1}\geq\left\lfloor\frac{5p_{s}+H_{L}+2(J_{L}-\kappa_{L}-1)}{4}\right\rfloor>\frac{5}{4}p_{s}. (61)

Every individual scale is nondecreasing. Along any consecutive mature good chain, the number NS​(T)N_{S}(T) of successes with common replay by TT satisfies

NS​(T)≤1+⌊log5/4⁡(1+T2​HL)⌋.N_{S}(T)\leq 1+\left\lfloor\log_{5/4}\left(1+\frac{T}{2H_{L}}\right)\right\rfloor. (62)
Proof.

Growth. After success, the POSM has one requester per occupied arm until the first fresh entry, even if business leases expire. Every replay request is accepted, so this entry occurs at

qs=mini⁡(Oi,s+Pi,s)≥Os+ps.q_{s}=\min_{i}(O_{i,s}+P_{i,s})\geq O_{s}+p_{s}.

Each next work invocation starts at or after qsq_{s} and lasts JLJ_{L} rounds. Warm output adjacency therefore gives

Δi,s+1:=Oi,s+1−Oi,s≥ps+JL−κL−1.\Delta_{i,s+1}:=O_{i,s+1}-O_{i,s}\geq p_{s}+J_{L}-\kappa_{L}-1.

Substituting Pi,s≥psP_{i,s}\geq p_{s} and this interval into (50) proves the first inequality in (61). Since HL+2​(JL−κL−1)>4H_{L}+2(J_{L}-\kappa_{L}-1)>4 and ⌊x⌋>x−1\lfloor x\rfloor>x-1, the second inequality is strict. Every actual output performs the update, so neither success nor coverage is required of the successor.

Count successes. Outputs in a counted episode precede TT, so (52) gives HL≤ps≤HL+T/2H_{L}\leq p_{s}\leq H_{L}+T/2. If NS​(T)≥1N_{S}(T)\geq 1, each of its first NS​(T)−1N_{S}(T)-1 successes has a completed immediate successor in the counted chain. Growth at those transitions and monotonicity through failures yield

(5/4)NS​(T)−1​HL≤HL+T/2.(5/4)^{N_{S}(T)-1}H_{L}\leq H_{L}+T/2.

This proves (62); zero successes are immediate. The additive one allows the last success an unfinished successor. ∎

Combining the episode counts.

For T≥2T\geq 2, combine Lemma 20 with (62). In a consecutive mature good chain of the final market,

Nfail​(T)+NS​(T)≤⌊QT2⌋+1+⌊log5/4⁡(1+T2​HL)⌋,N_{\mathrm{fail}}(T)+N_{S}(T)\leq\left\lfloor\frac{Q_{T}}{2}\right\rfloor+1+\left\lfloor\log_{5/4}\left(1+\frac{T}{2H_{L}}\right)\right\rfloor, (63)

where Nfail​(T)N_{\mathrm{fail}}(T) counts failures with common replay by TT. Thus the logarithmic maintenance term is paid once over the entire chain.

C.6 Concentration and Recovery from Statistical Errors

The preceding bounds apply to a chain of mature good episodes. We now bound the time until such a chain begins, using concentration and two cold recoveries. A maximal inequality at prescribed sample counts handles both adaptive sampling and random arm startup.

C.6.1 Adaptive Concentration

Let ℱt−1\mathcal{F}_{t-1} contain the history before physical round tt, and ℋt\mathcal{H}_{t} also contain current requests and acceptance decisions, before rewards. An accepted stream-xx reward lies in [0,1][0,1] with conditional mean θx\theta_{x} given ℋt\mathcal{H}_{t}. Rewards may be dependent across time, edges, and endpoints. Since conditioning on another endpoint’s current reward can change this mean, we analyze each player or arm separately as an owner receiving at most one sample per round, then take a union bound.

Lemma 23 (Time-uniform concentration for prescribed sample counts).

Fix an owner, two distinct streams, and deterministic positive integers n,rn,r. Weight the first nn accepted samples of the first stream by 1/n1/n, the first rr of the second by −1/r-1/r, and all other physical rounds by zero. Let XtX_{t} be the weighted centered sum through round tt and VtV_{t} the sum of squared weights. For every b>0b>0,

Pr{supt|Xt|>b}≤2exp{−2​b21/n+1/r}.\Pr\left\{\sup_{t}|X_{t}|>b\right\}\leq 2\exp\left\{-\frac{2b^{2}}{1/n+1/r}\right\}. (64)

For owner oo and a fixed family of at most KK streams, let Bado,a\mathrm{Bad}_{o,a} mean that some comparison in this family with positive counts is uncovered at the start or end of the round at local age aa. Then

Pr⁡(Bado,a)≤K⁡(K−1)2​a⁡(a+1)(a+2)5.\Pr(\mathrm{Bad}_{o,a})\leq\frac{K(K-1)}{2}\frac{a(a+1)}{(a+2)^{5}}. (65)

Both conclusions cover random arm startup times.

Proof.

A maximal bound at prescribed counts. Let wtw_{t} be the round-tt weight and, when nonzero, let Rt,θtR_{t},\theta_{t} be the selected reward and mean. The weight is fixed by ℋt\mathcal{H}_{t} before the reward, and truncation gives

Vt≤vn,r:=1/n+1/r.V_{t}\leq v_{n,r}:=1/n+1/r.

Conditional Hoeffding’s lemma gives

𝔼⁡[eλ​wt​(Rt−θt)∣ℋt]≤eλ2​wt2/8.\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\lambda w_{t}(R_{t}-\theta_{t})}\mid\mathcal{H}_{t}\right]\leq e^{\lambda^{2}w_{t}^{2}/8}.

Zero weights give zero increments. Conditioning successively on ℋt\mathcal{H}_{t} and ℱt−1\mathcal{F}_{t-1} makes

Mt​(λ)=exp⁡{λ​Xt−λ2​Vt/8}M_{t}(\lambda)=\exp\{\lambda X_{t}-\lambda^{2}V_{t}/8\}

a nonnegative supermartingale initially equal to one.

Ville’s inequality bounds the chance that this process ever exceeds exp⁡{λ​b−λ2​vn,r/8}\exp\{\lambda b-\lambda^{2}v_{n,r}/8\} by its reciprocal. Choosing λ=4​b/vn,r\lambda=4b/v_{n,r} and repeating for −Xt-X_{t} gives (64), using the ownerwise bounded-increment construction of [HRMS20]. This argument uses the conditional reward assumption, not independence between accepted samples.

Union over counts and comparisons. At counts n,rn,r, the truncated sum is the empirical difference error. Thus coverage failure lies in a maximal event from (64), without conditioning on realized counts or assuming conditional IID samples. With

b=5​log⁡(a+2)2​vn,r,b=\sqrt{\frac{5\log(a+2)}{2}v_{n,r}},

its probability is at most

2exp{−5log(a+2)}=2(a+2)−5/ln2≤2(a+2)−5.2\exp\{-5\log(a+2)\}=2(a+2)^{-5/\ln 2}\leq 2(a+2)^{-5}.

Each age-aa snapshot contains at most a+1a+1 observations, allowing a⁡(a+1)/2a(a+1)/2 positive count pairs n+r≤a+1n+r\leq a+1 and at most (K2)\binom{K}{2} unordered stream pairs. Their union proves (65). The same maximal events cover both snapshots without another factor of two. At age zero, two counts cannot both be positive; zero counts give infinite radii.

Random startup times. The process uses all physical rounds, with zero weights before startup and whenever no sample arrives. The supremum already includes the random round at each fixed arm age, requiring neither a union over startup times nor conditioning on them. ∎

C.6.2 Recovery after the Last Bad Comparison

To bound the expected sum of the last bad local ages, set

CY=K2​(K−1)4.C_{Y}=\frac{K^{2}(K-1)}{4}. (66)
Lemma 24 (The last bad age and two cold recoveries).

For a nonempty final population, almost surely a mature episode reaches common replay at R∗R^{*} with all remaining-set resets and work rounds after every bad comparison among the final players’ arms or between final players at an arm. All subsequent comparisons in these families are covered, and

𝔼​R∗≤94​(t∗+1)+52​CR+32​(1+CY).\mathbb{E}R^{*}\leq\frac{9}{4}(t_{*}+1)+\frac{5}{2}C_{R}+\frac{3}{2}(1+C_{Y}). (67)

The cost before R∗R^{*} includes all mismatch during recovery from earlier errors.

Proof.

The two recoveries have different purposes. The first bounds every arm’s startup time, converting a bound on bad local ages into a bound on bad physical rounds. The second resets the work states after those bad comparisons. Neither step discards permanent samples.

The oblivious schedule fixes the final identities. Comparisons by final players over their KK arms and by all KK arms over final players involve at most 2​K2K owners, including comparisons outside the restricted gap (11). Departed players’ records persist but leave requester sets after stabilization, so they do not enlarge this union.

Bound the last bad local ages. Let YoY_{o} be owner oo’s last bad local age, or zero if none. It is dominated by

∑a≥1a​𝟏​{Bado,a}.\sum_{a\geq 1}a\mathbf{1}\{\mathrm{Bad}_{o,a}\}.

Tonelli’s theorem and (65) give

𝔼​∑oYo≤K2​(K−1)​∑a≥1a2​(a+1)(a+2)5<K2​(K−1)4=CY.\mathbb{E}\sum_{o}Y_{o}\leq K^{2}(K-1)\sum_{a\geq 1}\frac{a^{2}(a+1)}{(a+2)^{5}}<\frac{K^{2}(K-1)}{4}=C_{Y}.

Indeed, a2​(a+1)/(a+2)5≤a/(a+2)3a^{2}(a+1)/(a+2)^{5}\leq a/(a+2)^{3}, and x/(x+2)3x/(x+2)^{3} is nonincreasing for x≥1x\geq 1, so

∑a≥1a(a+2)3≤∑a=14a(a+2)3+∫4∞x(x+2)3​𝑑x=898936000<14.\sum_{a\geq 1}\frac{a}{(a+2)^{3}}\leq\sum_{a=1}^{4}\frac{a}{(a+2)^{3}}+\int_{4}^{\infty}\frac{x}{(x+2)^{3}}\,dx=\frac{8989}{36000}<\frac{1}{4}.

Finite expectation makes every last bad age finite almost surely, without independence between owners or errors.

First recovery: start every arm clock. Apply Lemma 14 at v=t∗+1v=t_{*}+1. Regardless of errors, its root scan starts every arm by 32​(t∗+1)+CR\frac{3}{2}(t_{*}+1)+C_{R}; final players are born by t∗t_{*}. Let ZZ be the maximum of t∗+1t_{*}+1 and the last physical bad-comparison round in these families, using t∗+1t_{*}+1 if none. Thus

Z≤32​(t∗+1)+CR+∑oYo,𝔼​Z≤32​(t∗+1)+CR+CY.Z\leq\frac{3}{2}(t_{*}+1)+C_{R}+\sum_{o}Y_{o},\qquad\mathbb{E}Z\leq\frac{3}{2}(t_{*}+1)+C_{R}+C_{Y}.

Second recovery: clear inherited work states. Lemma 14 holds pathwise for every integer starting time. Applied at v=Z+1v=Z+1, it gives a mature episode with all remaining sets reset after ZZ and common replay at

R∗≤32​(Z+1)+CR.R^{*}\leq\frac{3}{2}(Z+1)+C_{R}.

Choose the least such integer round. Each candidate event is measurable in ZZ and the execution, so this countable minimum is measurable; set R∗=0R^{*}=0 on the null event of no candidate. Its certificates and all subsequent comparisons are covered. Taking expectations proves (67).

This pathwise substitution needs no stopping-time assumption, restart, or conditioning on ZZ. Both recoveries retain statistics, scales, and output records. Charging [1,R∗)[1,R^{*}) covers erroneous stable-edge deletions, inherited armed or root states, and incorrect injective long replays without rejections. ∎

C.7 Proof of Theorem 4

We combine the episode bounds from Section C.5 with the expected recovery time from Section C.6, including any final incomplete collection or work interval.

Proof.

Charge the finite prefix. First suppose the final population is nonempty and T≥2T\geq 2. On the probability-one event of Lemma 24, charge every round before R∗R^{*}. This covers the prefix if T<R∗T<R^{*}. Otherwise set S0=R∗S_{0}=R^{*} and follow the consecutive mature episodes from warm collection. All are good: remaining sets reset after ZZ, and later comparisons are covered.

Count episodes with common replay round Ss≤TS_{s}\leq T: a final output at T−1T-1 followed by replay at TT is counted, whereas an output at TT followed by replay at T+1T+1 is not. Lemma 21 bounds the cost on each interval

[Ss,min⁡{Ss+1,T+1}).[S_{s},\min\{S_{s+1},T+1\}).

These partition [R∗,T+1)[R^{*},T+1), including unfinished collection or 𝖶𝗈𝗋𝗄\mathsf{Work}. Equation (63) bounds their number, yielding

D⁡(T,I)≤R∗+CF​[⌊QT2⌋+1+⌊log5/4⁡(1+T2​HL)⌋].D(T;I)\leq R^{*}+C_{F}\left[\left\lfloor\frac{Q_{T}}{2}\right\rfloor+1+\left\lfloor\log_{5/4}\left(1+\frac{T}{2H_{L}}\right)\right\rfloor\right]. (68)

Appendix D Proof of Claim 1

Throughout this appendix, log\log is base two, while ln\ln and the relative entropies KL\operatorname{KL} and kl\operatorname{kl} use natural logarithms. We use independent Bernoulli rewards at both endpoints of every accepted edge, a subclass of the conditional-mean model. The protocol and arm-service rules are fixed before the unknown means are chosen. Rejections supply neither reward observations nor an exogenous ranking oracle. The argument also applies to a central controller that chooses feasible matchings and observes all accepted rewards, and hence can simulate the local protocol.

Lemma 25 (Information required by a one-edge alternative).

Let θ\theta and λ\lambda be static strict Bernoulli instances with the same population, differing only in one endpoint mean on an edge ee, from pp to qq, where p,q∈(0,1)p,q\in(0,1). Suppose ee is absent from the POSM of θ\theta and present in the POSM of λ\lambda. If the protocol is uniformly efficient on both instances, then

lim infT→∞𝔼θ​Ne​(T)ln⁡T≥1kl⁡(p,q),\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}_{\theta}N_{e}(T)}{\ln T}\geq\frac{1}{\operatorname{kl}(p,q)},

where Ne​(T)N_{e}(T) counts acceptances of ee, and kl\operatorname{kl} uses natural logarithms.

Proof.

Let θ\theta and λ\lambda denote two static mean instances with the same population and endpoint means μi,x\mu_{i,x} and πx,i\pi_{x,i}, as in Section 2. Let Ni,x​(T)N_{i,x}(T) count acceptances of edge (i,x)(i,x) in the first TT rounds. We compare the instances with identical initial local information and private handle orders. The full transcript records all proposals, acceptance/rejection decisions, accepted rewards at both endpoints, and the protocol’s parameter-independent random sources. Write ℙθT\mathbb{P}_{\theta}^{T} for its law and Dθ​(T)D_{\theta}(T) for the POSM-mismatch cost under θ\theta. Write KL\operatorname{KL} for relative entropy and kl\operatorname{kl} for its Bernoulli specialization. The random sources have the same law in both instances and contribute zero relative entropy. Conditional on these sources and the observed history, action and state-update rules are identical in the two instances. Thus the chain rule gives

KL⁡(ℙθT,ℙλT)=∑i,x𝔼θ​Ni,x​(T)​{kl⁡(μi,xθ,μi,xλ)+kl⁡(πx,iθ,πx,iλ)}.\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb{P}_{\theta}^{T},\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}^{T})=\sum_{i,x}\mathbb{E}_{\theta}N_{i,x}(T)\left\{\operatorname{kl}(\mu_{i,x}^{\theta},\mu_{i,x}^{\lambda})+\operatorname{kl}(\pi_{x,i}^{\theta},\pi_{x,i}^{\lambda})\right\}. (71)

For the one-endpoint change in the lemma, this reduces to

KL⁡(ℙθT,ℙλT)=𝔼θ​Ne​(T)​kl⁡(p,q),\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb{P}_{\theta}^{T},\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}^{T})=\mathbb{E}_{\theta}N_{e}(T)\operatorname{kl}(p,q),

because the other endpoint of ee and both endpoints of every other edge have unchanged reward laws. Only newly observed rewards contribute divergence; rejections and local state transitions contribute no additional term. Equation (71) specializes the adaptive change-of-measure identity to two observations per accepted edge; see also [KCG16, Lemma 1].

The assumed POSM memberships of ee give

Ne​(T)≤Dθ​(T),T−Ne​(T)≤Dλ​(T)N_{e}(T)\leq D_{\theta}(T),\qquad T-N_{e}(T)\leq D_{\lambda}(T)

pathwise in their respective instances. For a uniformly efficient protocol and every α∈(0,1)\alpha\in(0,1), the event AT={Ne(T)<T/2}A_{T}=\{N_{e}(T)<T/2\} satisfies

ℙθ​(AT)=1−o⁡(Tα−1),ℙλ​(AT)=o⁡(Tα−1).\mathbb{P}_{\theta}(A_{T})=1-o(T^{\alpha-1}),\qquad\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}(A_{T})=o(T^{\alpha-1}).

This follows directly from Markov’s inequality and the definition of uniform efficiency. Binary data processing and the bound on binary entropy imply

KL⁡(ℙθT,ℙλT)≥ℙθ​(AT)​ln⁡1ℙλ​(AT)−ln⁡2.\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb{P}_{\theta}^{T},\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}^{T})\geq\mathbb{P}_{\theta}(A_{T})\ln\frac{1}{\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}(A_{T})}-\ln 2.

Divide by ln⁡T\ln T, take the lower limit, and then let α↓0\alpha\downarrow 0. Using (71), we obtain

lim infT→∞𝔼θ​Ne​(T)ln⁡T≥1kl⁡(p,q).\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}_{\theta}N_{e}(T)}{\ln T}\geq\frac{1}{\operatorname{kl}(p,q)}. (72)

∎

Proof of Claim 1.

Fix KK and Δ\Delta as in Claim 1.

Original instance and unique stable matching. Let the players be p0,…,pK−1p_{0},\ldots,p_{K-1} and the arms 0,…,K−10,\ldots,K-1. Each player other than p0p_{0} will form a mutual first-choice pair with a distinct arm, leaving p0p_{0} its last choice. Reversing one arm’s preference between its owner and p0p_{0} changes the POSM; learning those comparisons will account for the lower bound. Choose player means

μp0,j=12+(K−1−j)​Δ,μpr,j={3/4,j=r−1,1/8+(j+1)/(8​K),j≠r−1,1≤r<K.\mu_{p_{0},j}=\frac{1}{2}+(K-1-j)\Delta,\qquad\mu_{p_{r},j}=\begin{cases}3/4,&j=r-1,\\ 1/8+(j+1)/(8K),&j\neq r-1,\end{cases}\qquad 1\leq r<K.

On each arm j<K−1j<K-1, set

πj,pj+1=12,πj,p0=12−Δ,πj,pr=18+r8​K(r∉{0,j+1}).\pi_{j,p_{j+1}}=\frac{1}{2},\qquad\pi_{j,p_{0}}=\frac{1}{2}-\Delta,\qquad\pi_{j,p_{r}}=\frac{1}{8}+\frac{r}{8K}\quad(r\notin\{0,j+1\}).

On the last arm, set πK−1,p0=3/4\pi_{K-1,p_{0}}=3/4 and πK−1,pr=1/8+r/(8​K)\pi_{K-1,p_{r}}=1/8+r/(8K) for r≥1r\geq 1. All means are interior and all local rankings are strict. In each pair (pr,r−1)(p_{r},r-1), r≥1r\geq 1, the endpoints are mutual first choices, so the pair occurs in every stable matching. The remaining player p0p_{0} receives arm K−1K-1, giving a unique stable matching.

The restricted gap. For this instance,

Ep0∗=𝒦,Epr∗={r−1}(r≥1).E_{p_{0}}^{*}=\mathcal{K},\qquad E_{p_{r}}^{*}=\{r-1\}\quad(r\geq 1).

Among the means of player p0p_{0}, the smallest positive difference is Δ\Delta. For each other player, the reward gap between its assigned first choice and any other arm is at least 1/21/2. At each arm jj other than the last, the only distinct players whose relevant sets both contain that arm are p0p_{0} and pj+1p_{j+1}; the difference between their means at this arm is Δ\Delta. The last arm belongs only to the remaining player’s relevant set. Consequently Δmin=Δ\Delta_{\min}=\Delta exactly. Gaps between low-valued options outside these comparison families do not enter the restricted gap.

A one-edge alternative. For each j<K−1j<K-1, change only πj,p0\pi_{j,p_{0}} to 1/2+ε1/2+\varepsilon, where 0<ε<1/80<\varepsilon<1/8. All player means remain fixed. The endpoints of the other K−2K-2 owner pairs remain mutual first choices. In the remaining market, p0p_{0} prefers jj to K−1K-1 and jj prefers p0p_{0} to its former owner, so (p0,j)(p_{0},j) belongs to every stable matching. The displaced owner receives K−1K-1, again giving a unique stable matching. The only matching edges that change are

{(p0,K−1),(pj+1,j)}⟶{(p0,j),(pj+1,K−1)}.\{(p_{0},K-1),(p_{j+1},j)\}\quad\longrightarrow\quad\{(p_{0},j),(p_{j+1},K-1)\}.

For Nj=Np0,jN_{j}=N_{p_{0},j}, Lemma 25 gives

lim infT→∞𝔼​Nj​(T)ln⁡T≥1kl⁡(1/2−Δ,1/2+ε).\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}N_{j}(T)}{\ln T}\geq\frac{1}{\operatorname{kl}(1/2-\Delta,1/2+\varepsilon)}.

The bound holds for every fixed 0<ε<1/80<\varepsilon<1/8, with the limit inferior taken first as T→∞T\to\infty. Since its left-hand side concerns the same original instance for every ε\varepsilon, continuity of kl\operatorname{kl} allows us to let ε↓0\varepsilon\downarrow 0 on the right-hand side.

From samples to mismatch rounds. Each acceptance of one of these edges in the original instance incurs a mismatch. All these edges share player p0p_{0}, so at most one can be accepted in any round. Hence

∑j<K−1Nj​(T)≤D⁡(T).\sum_{j<K-1}N_{j}(T)\leq D(T).

For fixed KK, the finite sum gives

lim infT→∞𝔼​D​(T)ln⁡T≥∑j<K−1lim infT→∞𝔼​Nj​(T)ln⁡T≥K−1kl⁡(1/2−Δ,1/2).\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}D(T)}{\ln T}\geq\sum_{j<K-1}\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}N_{j}(T)}{\ln T}\geq\frac{K-1}{\operatorname{kl}(1/2-\Delta,1/2)}.

The KL constant and logarithm conversion. For p∈[3/8,1/2]p\in[3/8,1/2], the second derivative of p↦kl⁡(p,1/2)p\mapsto\operatorname{kl}(p,1/2) is 1/[p⁡(1−p)]≤64/151/[p(1-p)]\leq 64/15. Its value and first derivative vanish at p=1/2p=1/2, so Taylor’s theorem and Δ≤1/8\Delta\leq 1/8 give

kl⁡(1/2−Δ,1/2)≤3215​Δ2<4​(ln⁡2)​Δ2.\operatorname{kl}(1/2-\Delta,1/2)\leq\frac{32}{15}\Delta^{2}<4(\ln 2)\Delta^{2}.

Converting the normalization in (72) to base two and summing therefore gives

lim infT→∞𝔼​D​(T)log⁡T≥(ln⁡2)​(K−1)kl⁡(1/2−Δ,1/2)≥K−14​Δ2.\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}D(T)}{\log T}\geq\frac{(\ln 2)(K-1)}{\operatorname{kl}(1/2-\Delta,1/2)}\geq\frac{K-1}{4\Delta^{2}}.

All alternatives change only arm means. The construction therefore proves Claim 1 even when all player means are revealed and accepted observations are centralized: the uncertainty responsible for the bound lies entirely on the arm side. ∎

Comparison with binary stability.

The constructed instance has a unique stable matching, so unstable-round loss and POSM-mismatch loss coincide on this family. In markets with several stable matchings, D⁡(T)D(T) also charges a stable assignment whenever it is not player-optimal; binary-stability loss does not [Bas25]. The comparison in Claim 1 concerns the logarithmic horizon growth and the inverse-square dependence of its asymptotic coefficient on the restricted gap used here: for each fixed KK and Δ\Delta, the lower limit is taken as T→∞T\to\infty.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
